summary: Reads a pair of 16-bit values from a linked list node at a given index. Validates a2 against the list length at this+0xC; on an out-of-range index it clears this+0x8 and skips traversal. Otherwise it starts this+0x8 at the head (this+0x0) and walks a2 steps following the next-node pointer stored at node+4. If the traversed node and its data pointer are valid, it copies two words into *a3 and *a4 and returns 1; otherwise it zeroes both outputs and returns 0. Used by sub_487060, sub_4870E0, UtilityFunction_7160 and TwoChannel16BitReader.

local_names.this: indexed linked-list container: head at +0x0, traversal cursor at +0x8, length bound at +0xC
local_names.a3: output pointer receiving the first 16-bit field
local_names.a4: output pointer receiving the second 16-bit field
local_names.v4: index copy used as the walk-down counter
local_names.v6: current node pointer read at this+0x8 during each walk step
local_names.v7: cursor value at this+0x8 reinterpreted as a word-pointer holder
local_names.v8: node data pointer (first word of the node) read from v7

operations.description: Index range check: if a2 < 0 or a2 >= this[3] (length at this+0xC), set this+0x8 to 0 and skip traversal entirely
Seed the traversal cursor at this+0x8 with the head pointer at this+0x0
Walk loop: while the counter is positive, read the current node at this+0x8, break if it is NULL, decrement the counter, and advance this+0x8 to the next-node pointer stored at node+4
Read guard: the node at this+0x8 (v7) must be non-NULL and its first word (v8, the data pointer) must be non-NULL before the fields are copied out
Success path: write *a3 = v8[0] and *a4 = v8[1] from the node data and return 1
Failure path: zero both outputs (*a3 = 0, *a4 = 0) and return the 0 result held in the result variable
Return 1 when both words were read, otherwise 0; the function is used by sub_487060, sub_4870E0, UtilityFunction_7160 and TwoChannel16BitReader

The next-node pointer at node+4 is dereferenced as a dword; the node layout beyond offsets 0 and 4 is not established
The length bound at this+0xC is trusted as-is; a NULL node encountered mid-walk terminates the walk early without updating the bound
